se: The subcommittee invited representatives of the Police Strategy Office, the working group on promotion assessment criteria under the Police Commission rules, and the Office of the Public Sector Development Commission to give information and exchange views on the weight of results indicators, developing KPIs that reflect the quality of the justice process rather than numbers alone, and measures to reduce unsuitable incentives. The subcommittee will gather the information for its study and make proposals to the government.
it: Study of the system and structure of the justice process as it affects state administration

se: The subcommittee invited the Eastern Economic Corridor Office (EEC), Regional Irrigation Office 9 and the Pollution Control Department to give information on water management in Rayong Province, so that there is enough water, used efficiently and in line with the area's development. The information will be used in the study so that agencies work together and are ready for long-term disaster risks.
it: Water resource management in Rayong Province

te: Justice system: police personnel and appointments
se: The subcommittee invited representatives of Provincial Police Region 1, the Central Investigation Bureau and the Cyber Crime Investigation Bureau to give information and exchange views on the study framework, staffing statistics of the Royal Thai Police, and transfers and appointments that affect performance. The subcommittee will gather the information for its study and make proposals to the government.
it: Study of the system and structure of the justice process as it affects state administration

te: Began studying the system and structure of the justice system
se: The subcommittee invited representatives of the Office of the Police Commission and academics from Mahidol University and Thammasat University to give information and exchange views on the roles, duties and powers of agencies in the justice system, the criminal inquiry system, problems at work, and the use of technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to support the work. The subcommittee will gather the information for its study and make proposals to the government.
it: Study of the system and structure of the justice process as it affects state administration

te: School safety and disaster preparedness in the Andaman coast provinces
se: The subcommittee studied ways to develop disaster education and safety in schools. It invited representatives of offices under the Office of the Basic Education Commission (OBEC), Ministry of Education, and of the primary educational service area offices in the 6 Andaman coast provinces of Ranong, Phang Nga, Phuket, Krabi, Trang and Satun, to explain emergency plans and drills in schools, the channels for reporting safety problems affecting students and teachers, and the safety criteria for school buildings. The meeting proposed adjusting the building safety assessment criteria so that they can be used in practice, and set Meeting No. 12/2569 for Thursday 26 November 2026
it: Putting the National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Plan B.E. 2564-2570 into practice in schools, for example a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation to develop disaster-management courses, and help centres for disaster-hit schools reaching down to district level

Channels for reporting problems with the rights, freedom and safety of students, teachers and education staff: the MOE Safety Center, the Traffy EDU system on LINE and the 1579 hotline; and emergency plans and drills for events such as fire, flooding and armed attackers
Safety criteria for school buildings and evacuation centres, covering the building structure, water and electrical systems, and facilities for older people and people with disabilities
Examples from the Andaman coast, such as tsunami drills with UNDP in 23 at-risk schools, and funds set up by educational service area offices to help teachers and students hit by disasters

A seminar on the subcommittee's work on 24 December 2026 at Parliament House, and Meeting No. 12/2569 on Thursday 26 November 2026 on the problems and obstacles in the command system and in joining up flood management

se: Representatives of the Thai Meteorological Department, the National Disaster Warning Center, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gave information on weather forecasting and monitoring, warnings, drainage and town planning, to find ways to reduce flood risk in Bangkok. Meetings were set for 22 and 29 October 2026.
it: Forecasting, warnings, drainage and town planning to cope with floods in Bangkok
Meeting dates: 22 Oct (disaster education) and 29 Oct 2026 (flood warnings in Bangkok)

te: Meeting summary video · Flood management in Bangkok
Disaster education and safety in schools
se: Representatives of the Ministry of Education, the Office of the Basic Education Commission, the MOE Safety Center and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation explained preparedness in schools, building inspections and the youth civil-defence volunteer project, as well as drills in schools.
it: Developing disaster and safety education in schools

te: Meeting summary video · Disaster education and safety in schools
Digital elevation model (DEM) data for water management and hazard-risk analysis
se: Representatives of the Royal Thai Survey Department, the Royal Irrigation Department, the Hydro-Informatics Institute and GISTDA explained how DEM data is produced and used, for example estimating flood levels to plan rescue of people affected, as well as problems linking and sharing data between agencies. The Ministry of Education and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation will be invited next time.
it: Producing, using and sharing DEM data between agencies
Education agencies invited to give information on safety in educational institutions, Meeting No. 7/2569

te: Town planning to reduce risk, the sponge-city idea and building safety
se: Representatives of the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning and university experts explained how hazard areas are used in town plans, building-control measures and the sponge-city idea, which has pilot areas with the Asian Development Bank in 5 provinces. The meeting also discussed the safety of buildings in earthquake-risk areas, with a proposal to consider cooperation between the agencies concerned.
it: Bringing disaster data into town planning and building control
Sponge city concept: pilot areas in 5 provinces
Safety of buildings in earthquake-risk areas, and a proposed memorandum of understanding between agencies

te: Military units using technology and geo-informatics to deal with disasters
se: The meeting discussed the role of military units in supporting disaster prevention and mitigation, working with civilian agencies and the use of technology, as well as the role of the Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency (GISTDA) in providing satellite images and geo-informatics data.
it: The role of military units and working together with civilian agencies
GISTDA's geo-informatics and space technology data for disaster management
